judgements.justification: A judged the paper as a neuroscience tool and rewarded its gains over BehaveNet; B judged it as a methods paper and asked what the stochastic model adds over its deterministic part.
The only score rise was U58y in B, a detailed expert reviewer moved by new experiments, and it stayed below threshold.
The committees read the paper as different kinds of contribution, which is R16, not one kind held to different bars.
A's only 8 (Reviewer_88jd) praised the model as 'thoroughly tested on two head-fixed mouse datasets', but WFCI appears in the main text only in Table 1.
U58y said its central interpretability doubt stayed unresolved and raised to 5; c1eX's concerns were not answered; no reviewer kept a score after its main concern was resolved.
A accepted promised ablations and fixes as future work; B's AC judged the changes needed too significant to credit for the camera-ready.
Reviewer_poVh agreed with the criticism in private but still supported the paper at 6; no stated stance diverged from a score.
No extra off-record reviewer appears in either committee.
Clarity was not a deciding issue; the split rests on what the model adds and on interpretability, not on exposition.
The only raised rating, U58y's, came with a stated reason and its text stayed consistent with a borderline reject.
No AC discounted a silent low rating; A had no low rating and B's AC followed all its reviewers.
A's only rating above 7 came from a one-hour review with no reply to the rebuttal, not a detailed checked reading or advocacy.
No reviewer in either committee admitted reading only part of the paper.
B contested what the stochastic model adds and the interpretability claim, not the premise from a different theoretical tradition.
A's meta-review gives generic praise, names no weakness and gives no reason for a spotlight beyond 'a very good piece of work'.
B's reviewers checked novelty against Yingzhen and Mandt [31], S3VAE and MoCoGAN and questioned baseline tuning; A took Table 2's comparisons at face value and focused on presentation and code.
B's AC named poVh in place of U58y, but the count of two reviewers against acceptance matches the record and poVh agreed with the criticism in private.
No reviewer or AC raised a narrow-audience or wrong-venue concern.
A had no low-scoring detractor, and B's low scores rested on correct readings.
Only B received new results ([31] baseline, view ablations, context-embedding accuracy), which lifted U58y to 5; A received only promised text.
Confidences were similar across reviewers in both committees, and no high-confidence expert was outvoted by low-confidence reviews.
No objection was added after the author response period closed.
A's verbal assessments were genuinely favourable and B's critical; the rating gap reflects different judgements, not scale leniency.
B judged the 'more interpretable' claim overstated, the authors conceded, and B's AC rejected partly on it; A took the claim at face value.
A's reviewers rated 7 and 8, above the marginal-accept level, and B's were below threshold.
